notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Psalm 142 this time. My first attempt to fetch the commentary pages all at once went over the tool's usage limit. After that, I wasn't allowed any more searches or page fetches. So I haven't read a single page from your approved sites.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for each point, and not to fill gaps from my own knowledge. With no sources read, any notes would come from memory, so I've left them all out.

If you ask again, I'll read the pages one or two at a time so I stay under the limit. I'd start with these, in this order:

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, then Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub, then Precept Austin.
2. **Protestant traditions:** Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (Baptist) and Wesley's notes on Psalm 142 (Methodist). Then I'd search the Reformed, Lutheran and Pentecostal sites for sermons or articles on this psalm.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes on netbible.org, and Augustine's sermon on this psalm on newadvent.org. His Bible numbered the Psalms differently, so he calls it Psalm 141. After that, the Orthodox and Catholic sites, and a check for any well-known prosperity or word-of-faith teaching on this psalm.

You could also split the job into smaller requests, for example verses 1–3 first, then 4–7. That would make it easier to finish.
